locations.description:
Volantis — the First Daughter

In the current Veil campaign, after the two-year time skip, Aurion Belaerys is the established Archon and ruler of Volantis, Lys, Myr, and Tyrosh. He took Volantis by rallying the Tigers and completed the takeover of the Three Daughters. His appointed triarchs, including Vaeron Belaerys, administer routine affairs under his authority.

At the mouth of the Rhoyne on the Summer Sea, Volantis is an immense, humid river port built around wealth, ancient prestige, and the labor of enslaved people. From the water it is a forest of masts beneath marble towers and black stone walls. Up close it is crowded quays, river mud, cooking smoke, wine, bells, shouted bargains, and elephants pressing through traffic. Its grandeur and its cruelty occupy the same streets.

The city in daily life

The eastern bank holds the old city and the Black Walls; the western bank draws sailors, foreign merchants, inns, warehouses, and markets. The Long Bridge is a busy street above the river, crowded with buildings, shops, and people. Trade connects Volantis to the Rhoyne's interior, the other Free Cities, and the eastern sea routes. Silk, spices, sweet red wine, and beet dishes belong beside harbor business and the countinghouse. A scene here can turn on a meal, a game of cyvasse, an introduction, or an ordinary purchase. The city has lives and pleasures beyond the business of its rulers.

The Black Walls and the Old Blood

The immense walls of fused black dragonstone enclose the privileged heart of Old Volantis. Residence within is the preserve of the Old Blood, whose standing rests on claimed unbroken descent from Valyria; outsiders enter by invitation. Palaces, gardens, ancestral possessions, and elaborate hospitality make lineage tangible. These families can share pride in their inheritance while disagreeing sharply about money, religion, marriage, public duty, and the future. Valyrian ancestry does not by itself establish descent from dragonlords. These customs describe the old social order. In this campaign Aurion has already won rule through the completed takeover; his office and command are established facts.

Government and influence

Before Aurion's takeover, three triarchs governed, elected annually from eligible members of the Old Blood by freeborn landowners, including women. The ten-day elections combine public celebration, personal influence, spending, and bargaining. Tigers favor martial strength and expansion; Elephants favor commerce and the wealth secured by stability. Elephant majorities predominated for centuries before the campaign changed the government. Those traditions shape interests rather than dictate every person's response: a soldier may prefer an affordable peace, and a merchant may support force that protects a route. In current Veil, Aurion is Archon. The triarchs he appointed, including Vaeron, carry out delegated administration beneath him; the former elected Hall is not his sovereign or a surviving source of permission over him.

Slavery, faith, and the streets

Enslaved people vastly outnumber the free and sustain households, transport, trade, and the city's armed order. Facial tattoos mark imposed occupations; the tiger stripes of slave soldiers make military authority visible. Wealth inside the Black Walls depends on this system, but people subjected to it have their own attachments, judgments, hopes, and ways of acting. Volantis contains many experiences of the same event. The immense temple of R'hllor stands outside the Black Walls, and the red faith has particular strength among slaves and freedmen; older Valyrian worship remains part of elite life. Priests, congregations, and households need not interpret an omen alike.

The memory of dragons

Volantis remembers itself as Valyria's foremost daughter. After the Doom, its attempt to dominate the other Free Cities ultimately failed; Aegon Targaryen's destruction of a Volantene fleet near Lys belongs to that history. A living dragon therefore touches both an imperial aspiration and a remembered vulnerability. Pride, wonder, caution, and practical calculation can coexist without immediately becoming a common policy.

Volantis in Veil — current government

In the current Veil campaign, after the two-year time skip, Aurion Belaerys is the established Archon and ruler of Volantis, Lys, Myr, and Tyrosh. He took Volantis by rallying the Tigers and completed the takeover of the Three Daughters. His appointed triarchs, including Vaeron Belaerys, administer routine affairs under his authority. Vaeron oversees treasury and fleet. Routine matters such as gates, harbor administration, accounts, and provisioning can be handled competently by the appointed government. The conquest is complete; the story now concerns what Aurion chooses to do with his rule. A fully grown Gaelyx and two newly hatched dragons are part of the current setting. Previous house arrest, Hall seals controlling Aurion's movements, and requirements for the old triarchs' permission to fly are historical restrictions superseded by this political change. A future challenge would require a new, specific action by an actor with motives and means, not an automatic reset of the government.

Portrayal guidance — possible responses, not events already decided

Let the city offer opportunities as naturally as complications. A Tiger might seek an honorable alliance or a share in future prestige. An Elephant might offer finance, shipping, or a dependable commercial partnership. An Old Blood household might extend sincere hospitality, a friendship, a marriage approach, or scholarly interest. A priest might seek a conversation; a sailor might simply want to see the dragon. Such motives can be mixed without making kindness fraudulent.

Build plots from particular people wanting things that matter to them, acting on what they could actually know, and responding to what Aurion does. Opposition needs a concrete interest, loss, fear, or duty behind it. Successful reassurance can settle a fear; a bargain can hold; an ally can help competently; a victory can leave room for enjoyment, discovery, or a new ambition. Give Aurion consequential choices and let their outcomes change the city. Do not replace a resolved obstacle with another examination or invent a betrayal merely to prolong tension.

relevantFacts.title: Free Cities — AWOIAF fact 1
relevantFacts.statement: The Free Cities, also called the Nine Free Cities, are a group of nine independent city-states in western Essos, located west of the Dothraki sea and the Painted Mountains and northwest of the Valyrian peninsula.

relevantFacts.title: Free Cities — AWOIAF fact 2
relevantFacts.statement: The Free Cities trade and interact frequently with the Seven Kingdoms of Westeros. Many in the Free Cities consider themselves more sophisticated than Westerosi, with some considering the people of the Seven Kingdoms to be savages.

relevantFacts.title: Free Cities — AWOIAF fact 3
relevantFacts.statement: The nine city-states composing the Free Cities lie across the narrow sea, east of Westeros, on the western side of Essos, the eastern continent.

relevantFacts.title: Free Cities — AWOIAF fact 4
relevantFacts.statement: Braavos, Lorath, Lys, and Tyrosh are located on islands, Myr, Pentos, and Volantis are located on the coasts, and Norvos and Qohor lie inland.

relevantFacts.title: Free Cities — AWOIAF fact 5
relevantFacts.statement: There are significant differences between the geography of the various cities, from the thick forests around Qohor, to the rolling hills of Norvos, to the tiny islands of Braavos.

relevantFacts.title: Free Cities — AWOIAF fact 6
relevantFacts.statement: Over the past two centuries, Pentos has fought six wars against Braavos concerning the practice of slavery and the lands located in between the two cities.

relevantFacts.title: Free Cities — AWOIAF fact 7
relevantFacts.statement: Four of these wars were won by Braavos.

relevantFacts.title: Free Cities — AWOIAF fact 8
relevantFacts.statement: The last war ended in 209 AC and in the peace accords, Pentos was forced by Braavos to make several concessions.

relevantFacts.title: Volantis — AWOIAF fact 1
relevantFacts.statement: Volantis, often called Old Volantis and the First Daughter, is a city in southwestern Essos.

relevantFacts.title: Volantis — AWOIAF fact 2
relevantFacts.statement: Located at the mouth of the Rhoyne on the Summer Sea, it is the oldest and the proudest of the Nine Free Cities.

relevantFacts.title: Volantis — AWOIAF fact 3
relevantFacts.statement: Volantis is one of the greatest, richest, and most powerful of these city-states, and despite depopulation by ancient wars it is still the most populous.

relevantFacts.title: Volantis — AWOIAF fact 4
relevantFacts.statement: While Volantis was, at the time of the Doom of Valyria, the mightiest of the Free Cities, in the centuries that followed Braavos cought up and rivals Volantis for power now.

relevantFacts.title: Volantis — AWOIAF fact 5
relevantFacts.statement: Volantis is key to the slave market, trading heavily with the cities of Slaver's Bay to the east. It is said there are five slaves to every free man in the city.

relevantFacts.title: Volantis — AWOIAF fact 6
relevantFacts.statement: Volantis use coins, called "honors", with a crown on one face and death's head on the other as part of their currency. The honors are no bigger than a penny.

relevantFacts.title: Volantis — AWOIAF fact 7
relevantFacts.statement: Volantenes are fond of sweet beets, which they grow in profusion and serve in most major culinary dishes in the city.

relevantFacts.title: Volantis — AWOIAF fact 8
relevantFacts.statement: They make a cold soup of the beets which is as thick and rich as purple honey.

relevantFacts.title: Yi Ti — AWOIAF fact 1
relevantFacts.statement: Yi Ti is a nation and region in Essos, east of Qarth and the Bone Mountains and bordered by the Jade Sea to the south.

relevantFacts.title: Yi Ti — AWOIAF fact 2
relevantFacts.statement: Nearby islands in the Jade Sea are Leng and the Isle of Whips.

relevantFacts.title: Yi Ti — AWOIAF fact 3
relevantFacts.statement: North of Yi Ti are the Great Sand Sea, the Shrinking Sea, and the Bleeding Sea; a great river runs south from the Bleeding Sea through Yi Ti to the Jade Sea.

relevantFacts.title: Yi Ti — AWOIAF fact 4
relevantFacts.statement: The realm of the YiTish civilization is the Golden Empire of Yi Ti, which was, according to legend, preceded by the Great Empire of the Dawn. Maester Yandel speculates that the YiTish civilization was contemporary with the realm of the Fisher Queens, whereas the YiTish priests insist that mankind's first towns and cities arose along the shores of the Jade Sea, dismissing the rival claims of the Sarnori and Ghiscari as the boasts of savages and children.

relevantFacts.title: Yi Ti — AWOIAF fact 5
relevantFacts.statement: Yi Ti was one of the earliest civilizations where literacy arose.

relevantFacts.title: Yi Ti — AWOIAF fact 6
relevantFacts.statement: The most ancient YiTish records are cherished and jealously guarded.

relevantFacts.title: Yi Ti — AWOIAF fact 7
relevantFacts.statement: Yi Ti is the oldest surviving continuous civilization in the world, having existed under one dynasty or another since the Long Night 8,000 years ago - other ancient civilizations such as the Ghiscari or Valyrians have long since collapsed.

relevantFacts.title: Yi Ti — AWOIAF fact 8
relevantFacts.statement: Lomas Longstrider once described Yi Ti as "the land of a thousand gods and a hundred princes, ruled by one god-emperor." Of old, the god-emperors were extremely wealthy and powerful, and commanded large armies.

relevantFacts.title: Westeros.org Concordance fact 1
relevantFacts.statement: The Free Cities speak a bastard version of Valyrian, as most have their origins as colonies of Valyria (I: 84. SSM: 1 )

relevantFacts.title: Westeros.org Concordance fact 2
relevantFacts.statement: Valyria left many roads, as old as a thousand years, that run straight as arrows on the eastern continent. These roads show no sign of wear or tear despite their age. Made of magically fused stone and raised half a foot off the ground to allow rain and snow to melt off their shoulders, the roads are broad enough to allow three wagons to pass abreast. (I: 193. V: 76, 77)

relevantFacts.title: Westeros.org Concordance fact 3
relevantFacts.statement: High Valyrian is still used by some (I: 603)

relevantFacts.title: Westeros.org Concordance fact 4
relevantFacts.statement: Dragonstone was the westernmost outpost of the Freehold of Valyria (II: 3. V: 76)

relevantFacts.title: Westeros.org Concordance fact 5
relevantFacts.statement: The Valyrians had great skill in shaping stone, although much of their knowledge is now lost (II: 3)

relevantFacts.title: Westeros.org Concordance fact 6
relevantFacts.statement: Valyria produced items known as glass candles, at least as of a thousand years before the Doom. They are said to burn with a light that does not flicker and casts strange shadows only under the influence of magic, or perhaps during portentous times. They are made of obsidian, twisted in shape with razor-sharp edges, and can be green or black in color (II: 638. IV: 9)

relevantFacts.title: Westeros.org Concordance fact 7
relevantFacts.statement: Some claim to still know the spells that must be used to rework Valyrian steel (I: 235. III: 359. SSM: 1 )

relevantFacts.title: Westeros.org Concordance fact 8
relevantFacts.statement: The Targaryens were on Dragonstone for about two centuries after the Doom before invading Westeros (I: 692. SSM: 1 )

relevantFacts.title: Westeros.org Concordance fact 9
relevantFacts.statement: There are descendants of the Valyrians scattered across the world. Many are in the Free Cities, most of which had their origins as Valyrian colonies, although they have become intermarried and mixed with other peoples (SSM: 1 )
